about.title: Arcadia Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a fatal crash happens on Baldwin Avenue, Santa Anita Avenue, or the Foothill Freeway through Arcadia, the family left behind faces grief alongside confusing questions about what comes next. Los Angeles County recorded 3 traffic deaths in Arcadia during the most recent final crash year, alongside 253 injury collisions — numbers that represent real households disrupted. California law gives certain surviving family members, generally a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, and in some cases other dependents, the right to pursue a wrongful death claim. These claims are separate from any criminal proceedings and follow their own civil timeline. We handle wrongful death claims for Arcadia families, reviewing what happened, explaining the options plainly, and managing communication with insurers so relatives can focus on each other during an already difficult time.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to specific relatives, typically a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents eligible in certain situations. We can help clarify where your family fits before any filing decision is made.

items.title: Awareness of Strict Deadlines
items.desc: Wrongful death claims in California generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window narrows considerably if a government entity was involved. Missing key dates can close off options permanently, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Clarity on What Can Be Recovered
items.desc: California law recognizes losses beyond funeral and burial costs, including lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a family can no longer count on. We can walk through how these categories apply to your specific loss.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none of these relatives exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible. We can review your family's situation to determine who has standing.

items.question: How much time do we have to file after a fatal crash in Arcadia?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If a government entity, such as the City of Arcadia or Caltrans, may be involved because of road conditions, that deadline can be much shorter. It's worth getting guidance early rather than waiting.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened near I-210 or Huntington Drive specifically?
items.answer: Corridors like I-210, Huntington Drive, Baldwin Avenue, and Santa Anita Avenue see a meaningful share of Arcadia's reported collisions, which can affect available evidence like traffic camera footage or agency records. We can look into the specific circumstances, including location and timing, as part of reviewing your claim.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they're separate matters. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action pursued by the family seeking compensation for their losses. One can proceed regardless of the outcome of the other.
